name: Abner
bio:
Abner was the son of Ner, Saul's cousin, commander of Saul's army, and the central figure who installed Ish-Bosheth as king after Saul's death, waged a long war against David's forces, and was finally assassinated just as he defected to David's side.

Abner served at Saul's side throughout his reign; when David slipped into Saul's camp by night in the wilderness of Ziph, he called out across the valley to challenge Abner for failing to guard the king (1 Samuel 26:5-16). After Saul and Jonathan died, Abner brought Ish-Bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over the rest of Israel, holding the real power himself (2 Samuel 2:8-9). When Abner's forces clashed with Joab's at the pool of Gibeon, Joab's brother Asahel chased Abner relentlessly; Abner, reluctant to kill him, warned him off several times but was finally forced to strike him dead (2 Samuel 2:12-23), earning him Joab's lasting enmity.

Later, after Ish-Bosheth accused Abner of sleeping with Saul's concubine Rizpah, Abner grew furious and secretly reached out to David, offering to rally all Israel behind him; David agreed to an alliance, on the sole condition that his former wife Michal be returned to him first (2 Samuel 3:6-16). Abner persuaded the elders of Israel and the tribe of Benjamin, then traveled to Hebron to meet David in person, who received him with a feast and sent him away in peace (2 Samuel 3:17-21). When Joab learned of it, he furiously accused David of letting the enemy escape, then secretly had Abner brought back and pulled aside at the city gate under pretense of private conversation, stabbing him to death in revenge for Asahel (2 Samuel 3:22-27). David, outraged, publicly cursed Joab's house and personally led the mourning at Abner's grave, weeping and lamenting, "Should Abner have died as the lawless die?" — and all Israel recognized the killing had not been David's doing (2 Samuel 3:28-39). Abner's death brought the long war between the houses of Saul and David to its end, clearing the final obstacle to David's rule over a united Israel.
